name: What are the biggest preconstruction mistakes homeowners make?

mainEntity.name: What errors cause the most delays and budget overruns before construction starts?
mainEntity.text: What errors cause the most delays and budget overruns before construction starts?

acceptedAnswer.text: The biggest preconstruction mistakes usually come from moving too fast before the project is defined. One major mistake is beginning design without a realistic budget range. Another is ignoring site conditions such as slope, access, existing structure condition, or utility limitations. These issues can change the project’s scope and cost quickly. Homeowners also run into trouble when they delay key decisions. If finishes, structural choices, or special features are not selected early, pricing becomes less reliable. Skipping consultant input is another common problem, especially when the project involves engineering, survey work, or permit complexity. A final mistake is treating the preconstruction phase as a formality instead of the most important planning stage. The more vague the scope, the more likely the project will suffer from change orders later. In Los Angeles, where local requirements and site complexity can vary widely, this matters even more. The solution is to slow down early and make decisions in the right order: feasibility, budget, design, consultants, permit strategy, then construction. That sequence gives the project a much better chance of staying on track. If a builder pushes you to sign before the scope is understood, be cautious. Strong preconstruction protects the owner by revealing problems early.
acceptedAnswer.description: The biggest preconstruction mistakes are starting design without a budget, ignoring site constraints, skipping consultant input, underestimating permit complexity, and choosing finishes too late. Another common mistake is failing to define scope clearly before pricing. These errors usually show up later as delays, redesigns, and change orders.
